standard_prerequisites.name: Functorial injective embeddings
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the functorial embeddings of the terms into injective objects out of which the replacement is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: Products of injective objects and their mapping properties
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Homology, the product rule for injective objects and the description of the relevant two-term complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply that products of the chosen injective objects are injective and that the maps out of the prescribed acyclic complexes into them vanish on homotopy, which is what makes the prescribed complexes redundant.

core_obligations: The construction (proof lines 1936-1948): for a complex the author forms a functorial complex out of products of the functorial injective embeddings of its terms and the prescribed acyclic complexes, with the comparison map defined by the functorial maps.

Functoriality and injectivity (proof lines 1949-1953): the assignment is functorial because all the data involved is functorial, and the comparison map is injective and factors through an injective subobject by construction.

The quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 1954-1956): the cokernel of the comparison map is the direct sum of the cokernels of the prescribed maps, hence acyclic, so the comparison map is a quasi-isomorphism, which is the second assertion.
proof_roadmap: Build the replacement complex out of products of functorial injective replacements and the prescribed complexes.
Read functoriality, injectivity and the factorisation off the construction.
Compute the cokernel as a direct sum of acyclic complexes to get the quasi-isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs functorially, for a prescribed set of acyclic complexes, a replacement of an arbitrary complex by one receiving a termwise injective quasi-isomorphism whose terms factor through injective subobjects and from which the prescribed complexes are homotopic to zero (statement lines 1921-1934). The proof is a complete construction: the replacement is assembled from products of functorial injective embeddings of the terms and the prescribed complexes (proof lines 1936-1948); functoriality, injectivity of the comparison map and the factorisation through injective subobjects are read off the construction (proof lines 1949-1953); and the cokernel is identified as a direct sum of acyclic complexes, which makes the comparison map a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 1954-1956). The non-formal content is the assembly and the cokernel computation. The claim is H2.
